what_it_does: This paper describes a neural processing unit (a specialized chip for AI) built into mobile phones to run AI models on-device. Unlike traditional phone chips optimized for image recognition with fixed patterns, this chip handles two very different AI workloads: large language models (LLMs like LLaMA) that need to read huge amounts of weights (mathematical parameters) from memory for each token (word piece) generated, and visual models (like Stable Diffusion for image generation) that perform billions of mathematical operations on data already loaded into fast memory. The chip uses a heterogeneous approach with different compute engines optimized for each workload type, plus a smart memory hierarchy that caches weights efficiently. Built in 4nm technology in Samsung's Exynos 2400 mobile SoC.
